mainTopic: קידושין through third parties (ערב and עבד כנעני), a woman who gives the money herself, and betrothing 'half' a person
overview:
This עמוד starts by finishing three cases of קידושין where the money does not pass directly from the man to the woman.
In the first case, the woman tells the man to pay someone else. She is betrothed, as we learn from an ערב (guarantor), who binds himself without getting anything.
In the second case, someone else pays so she is betrothed to a different man. That man is the husband even though he paid nothing, as we learn from an עבד כנעני who goes free with someone else's money.
In the third case, the woman has the man pay a third person and is betrothed to that third person. Here both sources are needed, and the גמרא shows that each one covers the weak spot of the other.
רבא then asks about a woman who gives the man money herself. מר זוטרא answers that with an אדם חשוב she is betrothed, because the pleasure of his accepting her gift is what she receives.
The גמרא explains why the guarantor and slave rules had to be stated both for קידושין and for money matters.
Finally, רבא rules that 'be betrothed to half of me' works but 'half of you is betrothed to me' does not. The גמרא compares this to רבי יוחנן's case of an animal owned by two partners, and says three lessons come from it, which are listed on the next עמוד.

steps.title: She is betrothed even though the money goes to someone else
steps.stepSummary: If a woman says 'Give a מנה to so-and-so and I will be betrothed to you,' she is betrothed. This is learned from the law of an עָרֵב (guarantor).
steps.simpleTranslation: '...and I will be betrothed to you': she is betrothed, based on the law of a guarantor. A guarantor gets no benefit, yet he still binds himself to pay. So too this woman gets no benefit, yet she binds herself and gives herself over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a case where the woman tells the man to pay someone else, and rules she is betrothed. It proves this from how a guarantor works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the woman receives the קידושין money herself. Here the money goes to a stranger, so she gets nothing. A guarantor also gets nothing (the loan goes to the borrower), yet he is fully obligated. So getting no benefit does not stop a person from obligating themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor, someone who promises to pay a loan if the borrower doesn't

steps.confusionAlert: The woman is betrothed to the man who PAID, not to the person who received the money.

phrases.english: "and I will be betrothed to you" – she is betrothed,
from the law of a guarantor.
A guarantor – isn't it that even though
no benefit reaches his hand –
he obligates himself?

phrases.aramaic: הַאי אִיתְּתָא נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב
phrases.english: This woman too, even though
no benefit reaches her hand –
she obligates and transfers herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a case that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who has the man pay a third party is betrothed to the man, learned from the law of a guarantor.

steps.title: Betrothed to a man who paid nothing himself
steps.stepSummary: If someone gives a woman a מנה and says 'Become betrothed to so-and-so,' she is betrothed to so-and-so. This is learned from עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Here is a מנה, and become betrothed to so-and-so': she is betrothed, based on the law of a Canaanite slave. A Canaanite slave loses nothing of his own, yet he acquires himself when someone else pays for his freedom. So too this man loses nothing, yet he acquires the woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second case: one person pays, but a different man becomes the husband. It proves this works from the freeing of a Canaanite slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the husband gives his own money. Here the husband pays nothing. When a stranger pays a master to free a slave, the slave gains himself without losing anything. So a person can acquire something with someone else's money.

phrases.english: "Here is a maneh, and become betrothed to so-and-so" –
she is betrothed, from the law of a Canaanite slave.

phrases.aramaic: עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי, לָאו אַף עַל גַּב
phrases.english: A Canaanite slave – isn't it that even though
he does not lose anything at all –
he acquires himself?
phrases.notes: Someone else pays the master, and the slave goes free.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי גַּבְרָא נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב
phrases.english: This man too, even though
he does not lose anything at all –
he acquires this woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case, the mirror image of step 1: now the man pays nothing instead of the woman receiving nothing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman can be betrothed to a man with money given by someone else, learned from the freeing of a Canaanite slave.

steps.title: When both the guarantor and the slave are needed
steps.stepSummary: If a woman says 'Give a מנה to so-and-so and I will be betrothed to him,' she is betrothed. This is learned from both the עָרֵב and the עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי together.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Give a מנה to so-and-so and I will be betrothed to him': she is betrothed, based on both laws. A guarantor gets no benefit, yet he binds himself. So too this woman gets no benefit, yet she gives herself over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third case in which the woman gets nothing and the husband pays nothing. It says both proofs are needed and starts with the guarantor proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here one man pays, a second man receives the money, and that second man becomes the husband. So the woman gets no benefit, which is the guarantor proof. The husband also loses nothing, which is the slave proof. This step lays out the guarantor half and sets up the question of why the slave is needed too.

keyTerms.meaning: From the law of both of them (both sources together)

steps.confusionAlert: In this case she is betrothed to the person who RECEIVED the money, not to the one who paid.

phrases.english: "Give a maneh to so-and-so
and I will be betrothed to him" –
she is betrothed, from the law of both of them.
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means the guarantor and the Canaanite slave from the last two steps.

phrases.english: A guarantor – isn't it that even though
no benefit reaches his hand –
he obligates himself?

phrases.aramaic: הַאי אִיתְּתָא נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב
phrases.english: This woman too, even though
no benefit reaches her hand –
she transfers herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the problems of steps 1 and 2 into one case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who has one man pay a second man, and is betrothed to the second man, is betrothed. This needs both the guarantor and the slave sources.

steps.title: The guarantor case is not a perfect match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the guarantor is really similar. In a guarantor case, the one who gains the guarantor's promise (the lender) does lose money. Here the husband loses nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But are they really alike? With a guarantor, the one who acquires his commitment loses money. But this man acquires the woman and loses nothing at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the guarantor proof alone does not fit the third case. This sets up why the slave proof is also needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a guarantor case, the lender gets the guarantor's commitment only because he handed over his own money. In the third case, the husband gets the woman without spending anything. That difference means the guarantor case cannot cover everything.

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
A guarantor – the one who acquires him
phrases.notes: This means the lender, who gains the guarantor's promise to pay.

phrases.english: loses money,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי גַּבְרָא קָא קָנֵי לַהּ לְהַאי אִיתְּתָא
phrases.english: but this man acquires this woman
and does not lose anything at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the guarantor proof from step 3 is enough by itself
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the guarantor alone as the source for the third case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a guarantor case the acquirer loses money, but in the third case the husband loses nothing, so the comparison breaks down.

steps.title: The Canaanite slave fills the gap
steps.stepSummary: The עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי proves that a person can acquire something without losing any money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Canaanite slave will prove it: he loses no money, and still he acquires himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by bringing in the slave case. It covers exactly the point the guarantor case could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slave gains himself without spending his own money. That proves the husband can acquire the woman without spending anything. Together, the guarantor and the slave explain the whole third case, which is why it says 'from the law of both of them.'
steps.whatToRemember:
There are three cases of קידושין through a third party:
Woman gets nothing: the proof is the guarantor (עָרֵב).
Husband pays nothing: the proof is the Canaanite slave (עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי).
Both at once: both proofs are needed. The slave covers the one point the guarantor cannot, that the acquirer lost nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that קידושין do not need the money to pass directly from husband to wife. A benefit can be given or received through other people.

phrases.english: A Canaanite slave will prove it,
for he does not lose money
and yet he acquires himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a second source to cover the gap
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The guarantor alone fails because the acquirer there loses money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slave proves a person can acquire without losing money, so the two sources together prove the third case.

steps.title: The slave case is not a perfect match either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a weakness in using the עבד כנעני as the source. In the slave case, the master who gives up the slave gets the money. Here, the woman gives herself up and gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the cases really alike? There, the one who gives up ownership (the master) is the one who gets the money. Here, this woman gives herself away and gets nothing at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the עבד כנעני proof from step 5. It shows a way the slave case differs from our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a slave, the master transfers the slave and receives the money from the outside person. With our woman, she transfers herself, but the money goes to 'so-and-so,' so she herself gains nothing. That means the slave case alone cannot prove our case.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? (a challenge to a comparison)

phrases.english: Are they comparable?

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הָךְ דְּקָא מַקְנֵי קָא קָנֵי,
phrases.english: There, the one who transfers ownership is the one who acquires [the money];
phrases.notes: In the slave case, the master gives up the slave and he is the one who gets the money.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא הַאי אִיתְּתָא קָא מַקְנְיָא נַפְשַׁהּ
phrases.english: here, this woman transfers herself
and she does not acquire anything at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם הָךְ דְּקָא מַקְנֵי קָא קָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the עבד כנעני support that step 5 brought.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using עבד כנעני as the source for the case in step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the slave case, the one who gives up ownership is paid. Here, the woman gives herself up and receives nothing.

steps.title: The guarantor fills the gap
steps.stepSummary: The ערב proves that a person can bind himself even when he personally gets no benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A guarantor proves it: even though no benefit reaches his hands, he still obligates himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by going back to the ערב. Each source covers the weak spot of the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערב binds himself even though the money goes to someone else, just like this woman. Together with the slave, who shows the receiver can gain without losing money, both halves of the case are covered. That is why step 3 needed both sources together.
steps.whatToRemember: The case in step 3 needs both sources: the ערב shows a person can bind herself without getting anything, and the עבד כנעני shows the other side can acquire without losing money.

phrases.english: A guarantor will prove it:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא קָא מָטֵי הֲנָאָה לִידֵיהּ
phrases.english: even though no benefit reaches his hands,
he obligates himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by pointing back to the ערב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining two sources so each covers the other's weakness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slave case alone fails, because the master is paid and the woman is not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ערב shows a person binds herself without benefit, so the two sources together prove the case.

steps.title: רבא asks about a woman who gives the money herself
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what happens if the woman gives the man a מנה and says 'I will be betrothed to you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if she says, 'Here is a מנה, and I will be betrothed to you,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. This time the woman gives the money to the man, which is the reverse of normal קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the man gives the woman something of value. Here the man receives money and gives nothing, so it is unclear whether a קידושין happened at all.

keyTerms.meaning: a sum of money (one hundred zuz)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction: here the woman gives the money to the man, not the other way around.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
'Here is a maneh, and I will be betrothed to you,'
what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question. It is related to the earlier cases, where money moved in unusual ways.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a woman betrothed if she gives the man money and says she will be betrothed to him?

steps.title: Mar Zutra: she is betrothed
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, quoting רב פפא, rules that she is betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said in the name of רב פפא: She is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given to רבא's question: the קידושין works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is stated with no reason yet. The reason comes out only in the next two steps, when רב אשי challenges it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra said in the name of Rav Pappa:
She is betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from step 8.

steps.title: רב אשי: that reverses the rule of land and movables
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that the ruling would mean land-type property is acquired through movable property. A משנה teaches only the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to מר זוטרא: If so, then land-type property is being acquired together with movable property. But we learned the opposite: movable property is acquired together with land-type property, through money, a document, or taking possession!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges מר זוטרא's ruling. He compares it to the rule of acquiring one kind of property along with another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי understands that the man acquires the money, and the woman is acquired along with it, like an אגב acquisition. A person is treated like land (property with אחריות), and money is movable (no אחריות). The משנה only allows movables to be acquired along with land, not land along with movables.

keyTerms.meaning: property that serves as a guarantee (land)
property that does not serve as a guarantee (movables)
money, a document, and taking possession (ways of acquiring)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Mar Zutra:
If so, it would be a case of
property that serves as a guarantee
phrases.notes: This means land. He is treating the woman like land here.

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת,
phrases.english: being acquired along with property that does not serve as a guarantee,
but we learned the opposite:
Property that does not serve as a guarantee

phrases.aramaic: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת
phrases.english: is acquired along with property that serves as a guarantee
through money, through a document, or through taking possession!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא: אִם כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's ruling that she is betrothed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the man acquires her through the money he receives, then land-type property is being acquired along with movables. The משנה allows only the reverse.

steps.title: Not אגב, but the honor of an important man
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that this is not an acquisition along with the money. The man is an אדם חשוב, and the pleasure of having him accept her gift is what she receives for giving herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think she said to him 'by means of [the money]'? Here we are dealing with an important man. Because of the pleasure she gets from his accepting a gift from her, she makes up her mind and gives herself to him.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא rejects רב אשי's understanding of how the קידושין works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי assumed an אגב acquisition, with the woman acquired along with the money. מר זוטרא says the money is just a gift. What actually betroths her is the הנאה she feels when an important man agrees to take her gift. That pleasure counts as value she receives, so it works like a normal קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: 'by means of / along with' (acquiring one thing along with another)
she makes up her mind / fully agrees

steps.whatToRemember: With an אדם חשוב, the honor of his accepting her gift counts as something of value. That is what betroths her, not the money itself.
steps.confusionAlert: The money here is not the קידושין money. It is a gift. The 'payment' she receives is the pleasure of the man's acceptance.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: מר זוטרא is answering רב אשי.

phrases.english: Do you think she said to him 'along with [the money]'?
Here we are dealing with an important man,
that with that pleasure
of his accepting a gift from her,
she makes up her mind and transfers herself to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining how the acquisition works, plus limiting the case to an אדם חשוב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woman is acquired along with the money, as in an אגב acquisition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The money is a gift. The pleasure of an important man accepting it is the value that betroths her.

steps.title: רבא: the same methods work for money matters
steps.stepSummary: רבא is quoted as saying that the ערב and עבד כנעני methods also work for money acquisitions. The גמרא then begins to explain why both rulings had to be stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated in the name of רבא: And the same applies to money matters. And it is necessary [to say both].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier rulings learned from ערב and עבד כנעני (steps 1-3) and applies them to money transactions. The final word 'וצריכא' sets up the next move: explaining why both the קידושין rule and the money rule needed to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא teaches that someone can acquire an item when the payment goes to a third party, or when someone else pays for him, just as in קידושין. The word 'וצריכא' warns us that the גמרא is about to show that neither rule could have been learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is necessary (to state both)

phrases.english: It was also stated in the name of Rava:
And the same is true regarding money matters.
And it is necessary [to state both],

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן מָמוֹנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבא's question about the woman giving money and returns to the ערב and עבד כנעני rulings, extending them to money matters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The acquisition methods learned from ערב and עבד כנעני also work for monetary acquisitions.

steps.title: Why the rule could not be stated only for betrothal
steps.stepSummary: If רבא had taught the rule only for קידושין, we might think it works only there, because a woman is happy with any small benefit. Then we would not apply it to money matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had only taught us about betrothal, we might say it works there because a woman is happy with even a small benefit, as ריש לקיש said: 'Better to be two than to sit as a widow.' But for money matters, I might have said it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of the 'why both were needed' argument. A rule stated only for קידושין would not teach us about money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קידושין, a woman wants very much to be married, so she agrees to be betrothed even through an unusual setup. That reason does not apply to money matters, so we would have doubted the rule there.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught us; he let us hear
She is content; it is pleasing to her
With anything at all, even a tiny amount

phrases.english: For if he had taught us only betrothal,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבא, whose rulings based on the guarantor and the slave were taught earlier.

phrases.english: we might say it works because a woman
is content with anything at all
in line with Reish Lakish,
as Reish Lakish said:
"It is better to sit as two bodies
phrases.notes: This is a popular saying: a woman would rather be married to anyone than be alone.

phrases.english: than to sit in widowhood."
But for money matters, I might say it does not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the 'why both were needed' explanation that step 12 began.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבא have to state the rule for both קידושין and money?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קידושין has a special reason: a woman agrees to marriage easily. So money matters could not be learned from it.

steps.title: Why the rule could not be stated only for money, so both were needed
steps.stepSummary: If רבא had taught the rule only for money, we might think it works only there, because a person can give up a money claim. That reason does not apply to קידושין, so both rulings were necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had only taught us money matters, we might say it works there because money can be given up. But for betrothal, I might say it does not work. So both were necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the argument and concludes that רבא really had to state both rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money can be given away through מחילה, even without receiving anything back, so an unusual setup works easily there. קידושין needs a real act of giving, so we would have doubted the rule there. Each case has its own weak point, so neither one teaches the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving up or forgiving a claim

steps.whatToRemember: This is a צריכא: each case has its own special reason, so we cannot learn one from the other. That is why רבא stated the rule both for קידושין and for money.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only money matters,
we might say it works because money can be waived,
but for betrothal, I might say it does not work,
so it is necessary to state both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of step 13 and closes the צריכא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rulings are needed: the קידושין rule rests on a woman's wish to marry, and the money rule rests on the power of מחילה.

steps.title: Betrothing 'half of me' versus 'half of you'
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if a man says 'be betrothed to half of me,' she is betrothed. If he says 'half of you is betrothed to me,' she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he says, 'Be betrothed to half of me,' she is betrothed. If he says, 'Half of you is betrothed to me,' she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא compares two wordings that both use 'half,' and they come out with opposite results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first wording, the 'half' is the man's. In the second, the 'half' is the woman's. רבא says only the second one fails, and the reason will come out in the next two steps.
steps.confusionAlert: Both wordings have the word 'half,' but they are not the same. One makes the man 'half,' and the other makes the woman 'half.' Keep track of whose half is being talked about.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he says, "Be betrothed to half of me," she is betrothed.
If he says, "Half of you is betrothed to me,"
she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling by רבא, not connected to the צריכא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Be betrothed to half of me' works. 'Half of you is betrothed to me' does not work.

steps.title: אביי asks: if not half a woman, then not half a man either
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the reason 'half of you' fails must be the פסוק, which says 'a woman,' not half a woman. But the same פסוק says 'a man,' so 'half of me' should fail too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: Why is 'half of you is betrothed to me' not valid? Because the Torah said 'a woman,' and not half a woman. So too, the Torah said 'a man,' and not half a man!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's ruling. He says the two cases should be treated the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumes the only reason 'half of you' fails is the exact wording of the פסוק. Since the same פסוק also says 'איש,' half a man should not work either. So the first case should fail too.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
What is different about "Half of you is betrothed to me"
that she is not betrothed?
The Merciful One said "a woman,"
and not half a woman.
So too, the Merciful One said "a man,"
and not half a man!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that 'be betrothed to half of me' is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same פסוק that rules out 'half a woman' should also rule out 'half a man,' so both wordings should fail.

steps.title: רבא answers: a man can marry two, a woman cannot
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that a woman cannot be married to two men, so 'half of you' fails. A man can marry two women, so 'half of me' just means he keeps the right to marry another wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: How can you compare? There, a woman is not fit for two men. But isn't a man fit for two women? And this is what he is saying to her: if I want to marry another woman, I will marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects אביי's comparison. He gives the real reason the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with 'half of you' is not only the wording. It means leaving the other half of her for someone else, and a woman cannot belong to two men. A man is allowed more than one wife, so 'half of me' is a real situation: he is only telling her he may take another wife.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejecting a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: 'Half of me' works because a man may marry more than one woman, so it only means he may take another wife. 'Half of you' fails because a woman can never be married to two men.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a 'half' in קידושין depends on whether a real half is possible. The question is whether the other half could belong to someone else.

phrases.english: He said to him: How can you compare?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, אִיתְּתָא לְבֵי תְרֵי לָא חַזְיָא,
phrases.english: There, a woman is not fit for two men,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the 'half of you' case. Her other half would be left for another man, and that is impossible.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא גַּבְרָא מִי לָא חֲזֵי לְבֵי תְרֵי?
phrases.english: but isn't a man fit for two women?
And this is what he is saying to her:
that if I want to marry another woman, I will marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by real-world logic (man versus woman)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases fail for the same reason: the פסוק says a whole 'איש' and a whole 'אשה.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Half of you' fails because a woman cannot belong to two men. 'Half of me' works because a man may have another wife.

steps.title: Let the betrothal spread through all of her
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא asks רבינא: when a man says 'half of you is betrothed to me,' why not let the קידושין spread to the whole woman? A ברייתא teaches that if someone makes an animal's leg an עולה, the whole animal becomes an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב מרי said to רבינא: But let the betrothal spread through all of her! Isn't it taught in a ברייתא: If someone says, 'The leg of this animal is an עולה,' then the whole animal becomes an עולה?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges רבא's ruling from step 15 that 'half of you is betrothed to me' does not work. He uses a case about holy animals to show that holiness on one part can spread to the whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With animals, holiness placed on one part spreads to the entire body. If that is true, then betrothal placed on half a woman should also spread and make her fully betrothed. That would make 'half of you' work after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it spread, so the effect on one part reaches the whole
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Isn't it taught in a ברייתא? This opens a proof from an earlier source
A burnt-offering, a קרבן that is burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Mari, said to Ravina:
But let the betrothal spread through all of her!
Isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
One who says: 'The leg of this animal is a burnt-offering'
then all of it becomes a burnt-offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִיפְשְׁטוּ לַהּ קִידּוּשֵׁי בְּכוּלַּהּ! מִי לָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling that 'half of you is betrothed to me' does not work
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that 'half of you is betrothed to me' does not work
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holiness on one limb of an animal spreads to the whole animal, so betrothal on half a woman should spread to all of her.

steps.title: Even the opinion that disagrees would agree here
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא adds that even the opinion that says the whole animal does not become an עולה only says so when the part is one the animal can live without. Half a woman is a part she cannot live without, so everyone should agree that it spreads.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even the one who says the whole animal does not become an עולה only says so when someone sanctifies a part the animal can live without. But if he sanctifies a part the animal cannot live without, the whole animal becomes an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא makes his challenge stronger. He shows that even the opinion that disagrees with the ברייתא would agree in a case like 'half of you.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal can live without a leg, so some say holiness on the leg stays only on the leg. But no one can live without half of their body, so holiness on such a part spreads to the whole. Half a woman is that kind of part, so the betrothal should spread according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says, meaning the other opinion
This applies only, which limits a rule to a certain case
A body part that life depends on, one the animal cannot live without

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין כּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה,
phrases.english: And even according to the one who says it is not entirely a burnt-offering,
that applies only where he consecrates
a part that the animal's life does not depend on,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ –
phrases.english: but if he consecrates a part that its life depends on,
all of it is a burnt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין כּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 18 so that it works according to both opinions
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that 'half of you' does not work
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Half a body is a part that life depends on, and holiness on such a part spreads according to everyone, so the betrothal should spread too.

steps.title: An animal is not like a woman with her own mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. An animal has no say in the matter, but a woman has her own mind, and the betrothal depends on her agreeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the cases really alike? There it is an animal. Here there is another person's mind involved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on מר זוטרא's comparison and says the animal case does not prove anything about a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's owner can make it holy all alone, so the holiness can spread on its own. קידושין needs the woman to agree. She agreed only to 'half,' so the betrothal cannot spread beyond what she accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? This rejects a comparison
There, meaning the case being compared
Another mind, another person whose agreement is needed

steps.confusionAlert: The animal case is not wrong. It is just a different kind of case. Holiness spreads in an animal because no one else needs to agree, but betrothal depends on the woman's agreement.

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There, it is an animal;
here, there is another mind.
phrases.notes: He means the woman herself, who must agree to the betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם – בְּהֵמָה, הָכָא – דַּעַת אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers by rejecting the comparison of steps 18 and 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between holiness of an animal and betrothal of a woman
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An animal has no mind of its own. Betrothal depends on the woman's own agreement, so it cannot spread beyond what she accepted.

steps.title: The better comparison: an animal owned by two partners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the right comparison is רבי יוחנן's case. An animal is owned by two partners. One partner made his half holy, then bought the other half and made it holy too. The animal is holy, but it cannot be brought as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is comparable only to what רבי יוחנן said: An animal belongs to two partners. One made his half holy, then bought the other half and made it holy too. The animal is holy, but it is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the leg comparison, the גמרא brings a case that really matches 'half of you.' Here too a second person, the partner, is involved. The next step finishes רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the half belonged to someone else, the holiness did not spread to the partner's half, because that partner had a say. This matches the woman, who has her own say. Since the animal's first holiness could not spread, the animal stays holy but can never be brought as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is comparable only to, which introduces the correct comparison
He made it holy, set it aside for the בית המקדש
And it is not offered, it cannot be brought on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that when someone else has a say, holiness or betrothal does not automatically spread. That supports רבא's ruling that 'half of you is betrothed to me' does not work.

phrases.english: This is comparable only
to that which Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
An animal belonging to two partners,
if one consecrated his half of it
and then went back, bought it, and consecrated it,
phrases.notes: He bought the partner's half and then made that half holy too.

phrases.english: it is holy, but it is not offered,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא דָּמְיָא אֶלָּא לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected leg comparison with a case that matches better
steps.raayaObject: That partial betrothal of a woman does not spread to her whole self
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling about an animal owned by two partners, where the holiness does not spread to the partner's half

steps.title: The Partly Consecrated Animal Can Make a Substitute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's ruling continues. The animal that cannot be offered can still make a תמורה, and the תמורה has the same status as the original animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it does make a substitute, and its substitute is like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יוחנן's ruling from the last step. That animal cannot be offered, but if someone tries to swap it for a regular animal, the regular animal becomes holy too, with the same limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said the animal is holy but cannot go on the מזבח. This step adds that its holiness is real: it is strong enough to create a תמורה. The new animal copies the original's exact status, so it is holy but also cannot be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute. If someone tries to swap a holy animal for a regular one, the regular one becomes holy too.
It makes a substitute. Its holiness passes on to the animal swapped for it.
Like it. It has the same status as the original animal.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that because the animal cannot be offered it is not holy. It is fully holy, enough to make a תמורה. It just cannot be brought as a קרבן.

phrases.english: And it makes a substitute,
and its substitute is like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote of רבי יוחנן's ruling that began in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The status of something made holy in parts, such as half a woman's קידושין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling about a partners' animal made holy in two stages. It is holy, cannot be offered, makes a תמורה, and the תמורה is like it.

steps.title: Three Lessons From רבי יוחנן's Ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that three lessons can be learned from רבי יוחנן's ruling. The lessons themselves are listed on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this three things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It says רבי יוחנן's ruling teaches three separate lessons, and it is about to list them one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is about to draw three separate halachic principles out of רבי יוחנן's ruling. This line only introduces the list. The lessons themselves appear on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it. This means a lesson can be taken from the ruling just quoted.

phrases.english: Learn from it three things:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the full ruling of רבי יוחנן (steps 21-22) into a list of lessons, starting with this opening line.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's ruling is a source for three separate halachic lessons, which the גמרא lists next.
